title: From GPS Points to Travel Patterns: Flexible and Semantic Trajectory Generation with LLMs

problem.claim: Large-scale, high-quality trajectory datasets are difficult to access because of privacy concerns.

gap.claim: Existing trajectory-generation methods do not explicitly capture travel patterns and generate only fixed-length trajectories under a single condition.

contributions.claim: HTP hierarchically generates travel patterns before generating GPS points using large language models.
A trajectory-specific residual quantization variational autoencoder quantizes micro-level GPS trajectories into compact macro-level travel-pattern tokens in a coarse-to-fine manner.
The method extends the LLM vocabulary with travel-pattern tokens and uses supervised fine-tuning to generate travel-pattern sequences under various conditions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two real-world datasets report that HTP outperforms the strongest baseline by an average of 29.78% in generation quality.
The authors report that the generated tokens capture segment spatial irregularities such as point-density variations caused by traffic conditions.
The authors report that code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Urban trajectories support urban-dynamics modeling and smart-city applications, but privacy concerns restrict access to suitable datasets.
Trajectory generation is presented as a way to synthesize realistic data, while existing methods lack explicit travel-pattern modeling and flexible conditional generation.
HTP first generates hierarchical travel-pattern tokens and then generates GPS points with an LLM.
The RQ-VAE produces compact macro-level tokens that capture spatial irregularities such as traffic-related density variation.
Experiments on two real-world datasets report an average 29.78% generation-quality improvement over the strongest baseline.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two datasets, evaluation metrics, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not report generation-length ranges, conditioning variables, or quantitative privacy-risk results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details sufficient to assess reproducibility.
